# Backlog

What is missing to go from "the hub can chat" to a usable family app, per area, in the order the
platform is built: the hub first, the robot for parity, Go last. A scannable list, not a narrative: reasoning and
decision history live in `docs/dev.md` and the records under `docs/plans/` and `docs/design/`.

- Check an item off only when it is shipped and verified (the org definition of done), not when it is started.
- A new gap found while working on something else is added here, never only mentioned in `docs/dev.md`.
- Size tags are a rough gut check: **S** (a session or less), **M** (a real slice, days), **L** (a platform-level
  capability, needs its own design pass first).
- An open row that has a design record carries a `Design:` line pointing at it; a row marked L with no `Design:`
  line is not pickup-ready until the record exists.
- Rows that are done and verified, obsolete, duplicated or in conflict with `docs/design/RULES.md` move to
  `docs/BACKLOG-HISTORY.md` with the reason; nothing is deleted. The last sweep was 2026-10-17.

## Reasoning reserve

- [x] **MAIPAI-CLI-01: `maipai start|stop|restart|status` for people who run Home** (S; built 2026-10-21; design `docs/design/maipai-control-cli-2026-10-21.md`, architect APPROVED). `scripts/maipai` (macOS and Linux), installed to `/usr/local/bin/maipai` by `install.sh`; stops Home then the Stack and waits for the engines, starts the Stack then Home and waits for the health answer, refuses during an install; tests with stubbed service managers in `scripts/maipai.test.ts`; user page `docs/user/maipai-command.md`. Follow-ups: MAIPAI-CLI-02 (Windows), the passwordless-sudo rule (owner decision), and the agent deny in RELIABILITY-PREVENT-03.
- [ ] **MAIPAI-CLI-02: the same command on Windows** (S, after MAIPAI-CLI-01). Objective: `maipai.ps1` installed by `install.ps1` with the same four verbs over the Home service, same order and plain-words errors. Acceptance: tests with a stubbed `sc.exe`/`Get-Service`, user page updated to drop the Windows line.
- [x] **SPOKEN-TEXT-01: the robot says times, dates and numbers the way a person does** (S, 2026-10-24; Jesse, live: asked the time, the robot said "3 thousand and 2 pm" for 3:02 PM). `backend/src/lib/spokenText.ts` (`toSpokenText`) turns clock times ("3:02 PM" is "three oh two P M", "15:30" is "three thirty in the afternoon"), dates ("Oct 23", "10/23/2026", "2026-10-23"), years ("2026" is "twenty twenty-six"), ordinals, money ("$4.05" is "four dollars and five cents"), percentages, temperatures, common units, phone-style digit strings, ranges and plain numbers into English words. It runs at the one shared boundary, `synthesizeSpeech` in `tts.ts`, so the chat read-aloud, a robot's speech, news read-aloud, the robot clips and the Wyoming server all get it; the stored and displayed text is never changed. Code, links, email addresses, version strings, hashtags and model names are left as written; a non-English locale is left alone; `opts.normalize: false` turns it off for a call. Tests: `backend/tests/spokenText.test.ts` (84 cases, idempotent, the real time and date sentences the robot says, and the Stack receives the spoken wording). Open: only English; a number with a unit word the table lacks is read as a plain number.

- [x] **REASONING-RESERVE-01: central reasoning room, one empty-length retry and ceiling guard** (S; built). Non-streaming calls share the reserve; streaming keeps its measured local ceilings.

- [x] **PHOTO-CHECK-01: photo inspector handles always-thinking models and unenforced JSON schemas** (S; built). Shared reasoning reserve, one larger retry, safe missing-age handling, and separate unreadable-photo copy.

## Chat answer images and safety copy

- [ ] **CHAT-IMAGE-HONEST-01: honest image results, article lead images and automatic named-subject pictures** (M; backend turn and answer image pipeline). An empty image result tells the model no picture was found or passed checks and asks it to offer retry or Wikipedia; the outcome is failed-soft `found_nothing`. Wikipedia page images lead for a resolved article, before ordinary Commons and search candidates. Written chat may start one lead-image pipeline from exactly one unresolved named subject, controlled by the existing picture preference and the normal age, surface and temporary-mode gates. Code is built; verification is blocked because the test preload cannot bind a free port. See `docs/design/safety-factual-references-2026-10-19.md` for the separate safety investigation.
- [x] **CSAM-TEXT-01: an adult's discussion is not filtered; depiction and generation stay refused** (M, risky surface: commons `spec/safety`, `nodes/safety.ts`, `outputGate.ts`; owner's ruling 2026-10-19; design [child-safety-text-2026-10-19.md](design/child-safety-text-2026-10-19.md); owner approved the rule 10 and SAFETY.md wording 2026-10-19). Objective: remove the minor-word-plus-sexual-word refusal from an adult's chat message and reply, as the leading assistants do; keep standalone explicit terms, a same-sentence request-to-generate check, every generation prompt and finished-media check, and every teen, child and robot floor. Slices: S1 spec signals, S2 hub gates, S3 docs and rule text. Acceptance: on the 86-text set an adult's chat refuses 0 of 45 harmless texts (today 24) and every explicit-term and request text; teen and child results identical to today. Status 2026-10-19: built: spec 0.1.192 (`csamMode`), hub `evaluateSafety(..., direction)`, rule 10 sentence, SAFETY.md bullet 1 reworded.
- [ ] **CHAT-SAFETY-COPY-01: explain an adult CSAM stream stop** (S; output copy only). Adult stream stops with category `csam` name the issue and give a safe next step. The blocked content and classifier are unchanged. Code is built; verification is blocked because the test preload cannot bind a free port.

## Birthdate removal

- [x] **MEDIA-HOME-01: the Media hub** (M; rebuilt 2026-10-20 after Jesse's review of the first tabs-only page). Home has a fixed Media rail destination (icon `cast`, never pinnable) that opens a hub: a Media column like Chat's (the kit's section sidebar) listing Home and the apps the person may use (Videos, Shows and Films, Music, Podcasts, Books), with the chosen app shown beside it. The apps stay standalone at `/apps/<id>`; the column appears around a media app only when the person came in through Media (`mediaHubSession`, a per-tab flag). `/media` is the Media home: pick up where you left off, new across the apps and recently played, from `GET /api/media/home`, which reads through the same access, kid and allowlist gates as the apps. Open: each app's look matches its counterpart in the mockup (`docs/design/assets/media-apps-2026-10-17/`), and an app-by-app audit against those screens is next.
- [x] **COMPANIONS-APP-01: the Companions app** (M, Home; 2026-10-21; record `docs/design/companions-app-2026-10-21.md`). `/companions` is a card gallery of the companions the person may use (type in plain words, four dials in words, who can use it) and `/companions/:id` the full companion (about, example lines, voice with a sample, who uses it for admins) with "Set as my default" (`persona.active_id`). Admins see each robot's companion with a link to its settings. Age rule is `companionFits`: child sees child companions, teen child and teen, adult any; above-type is a 404 on read, a 403 on write, a 400 on `PUT /api/settings`, and a stored pick above the person's type reads as the default in the turn. Backend `routes/companions.ts`, `lib/companionsApp.ts`, `tests/companionsApp.test.ts`; frontend `shell/pages/CompanionsPage.tsx`; screenshots `scripts/screenshotCompanionsApp.ts`. Reachable from All apps and pinnable; not a permanent rail icon.
- [ ] **COMPANIONS-MULTI-01: many companions per person, switching, and the companion across the app** (L; research and design first, no build; design record written 2026-10-24: [companions-shared-chat-and-presence-2026-10-24.md](design/companions-shared-chat-and-presence-2026-10-24.md), architect APPROVED and the owner's seven decisions recorded in its section 13 on 2026-10-24; phase 0 is the coming-soon shells, COMPANIONS-SHELL-01). Jesse's ask: a person can have several companions and switch between them, like Grok's companions. Examples: one that does shopping and another that is just a chat buddy; one chat buddy for research and another for casual talk. He also wants the companion integrated into the chat and possibly into the rest of the app, which needs mapping out. Open questions for the research: how comparable products (Grok companions, Character.AI, Replika, ChatGPT personas and custom GPTs) let a person hold and switch companions; whether a companion is tied to a task, a mood or a conversation; how it interacts with the existing default companion, the per-person companion choice, memory, voice, the age and surface gates, and the video avatar in the chat corner (CMEDIA-PLAYER-01); where in the app a companion appears beyond chat. Output is a design record under `docs/design/` and an architect verdict before any slice is built. Related: COMPANIONS-APP-01, COMPANIONS-STUDIO-01.

    Built 2026-10-21 (second pass): the editor's **Look tab**, in four slices. **CMEDIA-LOOK-01** (a picture store per companion under its data folder, upload with background removal, the look routes), **CMEDIA-LOOK-02** (four candidates from the look prompt through the picture engine, change a picture with words, a key-colour cut-out), **CMEDIA-LOOK-03** (the character sheet: three side views, a description card, the key colour, approval) and **CMEDIA-LOOK-04** (the Look tab page). Screenshots opened and judged on a scratch hub with uploaded pictures. **Not exercised against a real picture engine:** generate, change-with-words and the sheet's side views are tested with a faked Stack only; the scratch hub has no picture model, so the first real run is still owed (a person with the picture model installed generates four candidates and makes a sheet). Real-person uploads are refused for now (the likeness path is a later row). Still open: the states grid and clips (CMEDIA-EDITOR-04), the audience review screen (CMEDIA-EDITOR-05), the player, render, review and bundle rows, and the key-colour bench (CMEDIA-BENCH-01).
    Built 2026-10-21 (third pass): the editor's **States tab**, in five slices. **CMEDIA-STACK-01** (Stack repo: the media job `media.companion_clip` finishes a clip: cuts the background out, fits a loop, scales to 480, stacks premultiplied colour over an alpha matte, encodes H.264 and AV1, writes a measured `report.json`; landed at Stack commit 7bb13f3, pinned in Home's installer), **CMEDIA-STATES-01** (a per-state clip store in each companion's folder, the media folder declaration to the Stack, the finishing call, clip upload, approval that writes the manifest `animation` block and a flat `animation/` folder, clip files served with byte ranges), **CMEDIA-STATES-02** (up to four candidate clips per state through the video model from the rest picture on the key colour, one at a time, the best take chosen by the report), **CMEDIA-STATES-03** (the States tab: twelve cards, motion sentences, make or upload clips, takes with their measured numbers in words, preview over a checkerboard through a small WebGL shader, approve). Evidence: the Stack job was run end to end on synthetic clips on both key colours and a frame was opened (premultiplied red on top, white matte below; a first version came out grey and was fixed); the page was opened on a scratch hub with a seeded clip and the shader drew the clip transparent over the checkerboard in a browser with WebGL. **Not exercised for real:** a clip from the actual video model (Wan2.2 on a key-colour start picture), the pinned jellyfin-ffmpeg (the tests used a bundled ffmpeg 7.1), the AV1 encode on the pinned build, and a real browser (not headless) playing AV1 or H.264. The **key-colour bench (CMEDIA-BENCH-01) is therefore still owed and now cheap**: make clips of three characters and read each take's `report.json`. Limits of this version: the Stack must be on the same computer (the media job reads files by path); real-person clips are refused; the first-guess quality limits (`COMPANION_CLIP_LIMITS`) are not yet calibrated. Still open: the audience review screen (CMEDIA-EDITOR-05), the kit player and the `Avatar` state machine (CMEDIA-PLAYER-01), review and bundle rows (CMEDIA-REVIEW-01, CMEDIA-BUNDLE-01), the likeness path for real-person pictures and clips.

- [ ] **BIRTHDATE-REMOVE-01: remove birthdate from decisions and ordinary People editing** (M; first part built, 2026-10-18). Home forms use role choices only. People APIs accept and ignore legacy date input, and missing dates are tolerated. Automatic birthday role changes are disabled, including existing scheduled jobs. Legacy import accepts dates without requiring or saving them; unmatched legacy users need a role-selected Home profile unless their legacy role explicitly says admin. The pinned Person spec already makes birthdate optional and nullable; no spec change in this slice. Remaining: remove the stored column through a separately approved migration and remove the spec field with a later spec tag and consumer updates; external image-subject checks remain a separate safety slice. ## Content protections shared by every feature

Design: [one definition per person](design/content-policy-2026-10-18.md). Architect verdict for all rows: proposed: APPROVED-WITH-CONDITIONS; architect agent has not ruled. Every row needs independent minor-safety review and a full `bash scripts/check.sh` before shipping. No rule changes in these slices. Order: 01, 02, 03, LIKENESS-SIMPLIFY-01, 04, 05.

- [x] **CONTENT-POLICY-01: one synchronous per-person protection module** (M; first). ## Setup and the first run

- [x] **CANARY-01: behavioural canaries, one shared schedule and prewarm** (L, built 2026-10-17; first live run on the Studio: embed, voice loopback, chat hello and picture read passed, the search check failed as expected; open: `video_tiny`, a Stack route for `requestEngineRestart` so a dead chat can be restarted once, and tuning intervals from a week of recorded first-token times). Jesse, 2026-10-17: "why can I find quickly that something is broken and you don't know?" A built-in non-person health identity runs the real chat pipeline in temporary mode and asserts behaviour (hello, weather tool call, search tool call, picture read, embed, TTS/STT loopback, spoken turn, tiny picture on demand); 2 failures in a row raise one Repairs item per check; Status row "Last checked"; Run checks now; Keep the AI warm switch.

- [ ] **SELFHEAL-01: engine self-heal, circuit breaker, LaunchAgent and Home watcher** (L; Stack repo, owned by the self-heal session). Design: [reliability-2026-10-17](design/reliability-2026-10-17.md)
- [ ] **RELIABILITY-PREVENT-01: a turn is never cancelled by the 60 second replay timer** (S, Home). Jesse's live turn "Give me a few ideas for a fun weekend at home." ended "cancelled" after 60.3 s: `RESUME_TTL_MS` (`backend/src/routes/turn.ts:61`) aborts every unfinished turn because its timer is armed at turn start (`turn.ts:1054`). Arm it when the turn reaches a terminal state. Acceptance: a test with a fake engine that answers after 70 s completes with text; the replay buffer still expires 60 s after the end. Design: [reliability-2026-10-17](design/reliability-2026-10-17.md), section "Root causes seen 2026-10-17 and prevention". Exit: `scripts/check.sh --pre`.
- [ ] **RELIABILITY-PREVENT-02: engines ignore stray signals** (S, Stack repo). Every unexpected engine stop on 2026-10-17 was a `pkill` or `kill` from an agent (14:48, 00:49). Start engine children through `sh -c 'trap "" TERM INT HUP; exec ...'` and stop them with SIGKILL after a drain. Files: `stack/backend/src/lib/supervisor.ts`. Acceptance: `kill -TERM` and `pkill -f llama-server` on a test Stack leave every role ready; a Stack stop and a role restart still end the process. Design: same note.
- [ ] **RELIABILITY-PREVENT-03: agent guard for live-machine commands** (S, `.github`). Hook beside `origin-guard.sh` that denies `pkill`/`killall` with `-f` or any operand after the first (macOS reads extra operands as patterns; `-u` matched llama-server's `-ub`), `launchctl kickstart|bootout|bootstrap` on `com.maipai.*`, `sudo maipai-install`, and non-GET calls to `:8770` or `:3000` unless the command sets `ALLOW_LIVE=1`; the denial names the rule and the safe form. Files: `standards/bin/live-guard.sh`, the shared plugin hooks. Acceptance: each denied form fails by name in a test; `pkill -u 501 -f pattern` is not flagged. MAIPAI-CLI-01 addition (2026-10-21): the hook also denies `maipai stop`, `maipai start` and `maipai restart` (not `maipai status`) unless the command sets `ALLOW_LIVE=1`, or agents could use the new command around the guard. Design: same note.
- [ ] **RELIABILITY-PREVENT-04: the Stack's mutating routes need a Home credential** (M, Stack repo plus Home). `stack/backend/src/app.ts` has no authentication ("loopback is the whole authentication"). Token written 0600 by the installer, held in Home's credential store, sent as a header on engine stop/start/restart, settings PUT/apply, components, updates and job cancel; reads, `/healthz` and `/v1/*` generation stay open. Files: `stack/backend/src/app.ts`, `routes/engines.ts`, `settings.ts`, `components.ts`, `updates.ts`, `jobs.ts`, Home `lib/stack/`, `docs/CREDENTIALS.md`. Acceptance: an unauthenticated `POST /stack/v1/engines/chat/stop` returns 401 with the fix in words; Home still works after an upgrade. Design: same note.
- [ ] **RELIABILITY-PREVENT-05: dev Homes and scripts refuse the live Stack port** (S, Home). `stackUrl()` (`backend/src/lib/ports.ts:20`) throws by name when the data directory is not the live one and the URL resolves to 8770, unless `MAIPAI_ALLOW_LIVE_STACK=1`; `scripts/gate/shardTests.ts:247` and the proof scripts default to a stub. Acceptance: a test Home with `engines.stack.url` set to 8770 fails at start with the variable named. Design: same note.
- [ ] **RELIABILITY-PREVENT-06: a turn that loses its engine mid-stream is retried once after the heal** (M, Home). On `engine_unavailable` or "stream ended before the engine finished", wait for the role to be ready (self-heal takes 2 to 15 s), run the model node once more with the same context, then show the existing calm error. Files: `backend/src/lib/turnMachine/nodes/model.ts` (`runOneGeneration`), `turnNext.ts:1055`. Acceptance: a fake engine killed mid-stream and restarted gives the person an answer with no error line. Design: same note.
- [ ] **RELIABILITY-PREVENT-07: admission priorities in the memory governor** (M, Stack repo). chat > voice > memory judge > picture and video: never unload voice or the judge within 5 minutes of a conversation; a video or picture job waits while a chat request is in flight or the level is warn or worse, and Status says why. Seven `critical` events on 2026-10-17 evicted the judge or voice; a 125 s video job overlapped the cancelled turn. Files: `stack/backend/src/lib/memoryWatchdog.ts`, `lib/supervisor.ts`, `routes/jobs.ts`. Acceptance: a recorded memory trace with a chat request keeps voice and judge loaded and the video job queued. Design: same note.
- [ ] **RELIABILITY-PREVENT-08: name an outside stop and alert on repeated unknown exits** (S, Stack repo plus Home). An `engine.exit` with code 0, no signal and no supervisor request on two or more roles within 5 s is `external_stop`, outside the circuit breaker, with one Repairs item "Something outside MaiPai stopped the engines"; three `unknown` exits for one role in 30 minutes raise "engine keeps stopping". Files: `stack/backend/src/lib/selfHeal.ts`, `supervisor.ts`, Home Repairs mapping. Acceptance: replaying the 00:49:51 log lines produces the one Repairs item. Design: same note.
- [ ] **RELIABILITY-PREVENT-09: dev-load discipline and a reaper for leaked test processes** (S, `.github`). `wt.sh reap` lists, and after an hour kills, processes under `wt/*` or a scratchpad that hold more than 12 GB or are leftovers (`data-test/run-*`, about 12 pocket-tts processes since 12:17); the Stack test harness kills its children through a process group. Evidence: bun at 43.9 GB and python at 29.4 GB beside the live Stack at the `critical` events. Files: `standards/bin/wt.sh`, `stack/backend/tests`. Acceptance: a finished test run leaves no child; reap lists the offenders by size and cwd. Design: same note.

## Hardware tiers (2026-09-23)

The hub installs on what a family has; the Studio is the p128 profile with 128 GB memory and a 2 TB internal disk, the top of the range, not the baseline. The design is [docs/plans/hardware-tiers-2026-09-23.md](plans/hardware-tiers-2026-09-23.md): four reference points (the floor, a 24 GB Apple silicon laptop and a p128 Studio with 128 GB memory and 2 TB internal disk, a 16 GB CUDA laptop, a 128 GB Studio and up), one pipeline, only the budget record and the deployment limits varying, and a configuration that is proposed by the Stack's probe and stepped down by the person, never fixed. The order among voice, photos and pictures is the owner's. The Stack's own rows (STACK-SIZE-01, STACK-FLOOR-01) are in `stack/docs/BACKLOG.md`.

## Studio day one (2026-09-23)

A month of lead time is prework time: stage, script and dry-run now so the Studio downloads nothing large, runs a checked runbook, evaluates its own configuration, and becomes a coding lane. The design record is [docs/plans/studio-day-one-2026-09-23.md](plans/studio-day-one-2026-09-23.md); its numbered questions are the owner's.

- [ ] **STUDIO-STAGE-01: the staging kit** (M, Sonnet). Objective: `scripts/studio/stage.sh` fetches every day-one artifact by its pinned URL and verifies its sha256 through the Stack's own download code (`stack/backend/src/lib/download.ts`), writing the Stack's store layout onto an external drive with a `STAGE.md` of every hash and size, and `--verify` re-hashes the drive; `--install <drive>` copies it into place. Items: llama-server b10797 macOS arm64, Qwen3.8-27B and Qwen3.6-35B-A3B as GGUF at Q6 at pinned revisions, the two Splash packages (17.4 GB and 20.9 GB, pre-seeded into the Hugging Face cache layout; the package is proprietary, 4-bit weights with the vision encoder and the draft in one file that only Splash loads, so the GGUF cannot stand in for it and both forms are staged on purpose), the MLX-format weights of both candidates at pinned revisions for oMLX and mlx-serve, the pins the installer and the Stack already carry. Acceptance: `--verify` green on this Mac's drive; a dry run proves whether `splash serve` honours the pre-seeded cache with the network denied, recorded either way; the Splash formula revision in `STAGE.md` (the Studio ships with macOS 26.4, decision 1 of the record, so no macOS contingency). Out of scope: any model not in MEASURE-02. Exit: `bash scripts/check.sh` and `STAGE.md`.
    Design: [studio-day-one-2026-09-23](plans/studio-day-one-2026-09-23.md)
- [ ] **STUDIO-RUNBOOK-01: the runbook, unboxing to the acceptance workload** (M, Sonnet). Objective: the record's eleven steps as a checked document (`docs/dev/studio-runbook.md`), each with its command and its check, a target under two hours; every scriptable step gains a `--dry-run` flag (`scripts/install.sh` has one) and is run on this Mac now with its output recorded. Acceptance: the dry run of every scriptable step recorded in dev.md; the restore step rehearsed against a fresh data directory from this Mac's latest backup. Out of scope: the evaluation (STUDIO-EVAL-01). Exit: `bash scripts/check.sh --docs` and the recorded dry run.
    Design: [studio-day-one-2026-09-23](plans/studio-day-one-2026-09-23.md)
- [ ] **STUDIO-EVAL-01: the Studio evaluates its own configuration** (M, Sonnet). Objective: `scripts/studio/evaluate.sh` chains, on a scratch data directory, the Stack's Studio bench protocol (`stack/scripts/bench/studio-bench.sh`), ENGINE-CONTRACT-01's suite per engine (the set is four: llama-server, oMLX, mlx-serve and Splash, each through the same suite, the same MEASURE-02 rows and the same workload; the summary picks by the numbers and the contract, never by a headline claim, and an engine that loses on chat keeps its own role: oMLX's SSD prefix cache for long companion contexts, mlx-serve's media roles), ENGINE-SPLASH-01, MEASURE-02's rows per candidate with llama-server run with the model's MTP head on and every latency measured cold and warm at 32K with the effective rate from send to last token, and STUDIO-ACCEPT-01's workload with first useful answer cold and warm, collecting the summary rows into one `report.md` in the protocol's shape and appending them to dev.md "Measured so far", so a Claude session reads tables. Mirror: `studio-bench.sh`. Acceptance: a rehearsal on this Mac (tier 1, the 8B) runs end to end and writes the report with the rehearsal marked as such; the report's summary names the candidate that passes the contract suite, clears the tool-calling bars and gives the best first useful answer under the workload. Exit: `bash scripts/check.sh` and the rehearsal report.
    Design: [studio-day-one-2026-09-23](plans/studio-day-one-2026-09-23.md)
- [ ] **STUDIO-LANE-01: the Studio as a coding lane** (M, Sonnet; after STUDIO-EVAL-01). Objective: the coordinator's OpenCode HTTP driver pointed at the Studio's engine, with the lane rules from the record: a fresh session and a fresh worktree per brief at the base the coordinator names, deleted after the report; a wall-clock budget (three times a reference run) in place of a step count and a run that ends without a done report counted as blocked; the tool set the brief names (read, edit, the named tests, commit, never push); S and M coding items, second reviews by a different model, the benches. `splash claude` proven on the Studio before Claude Code is routed to it (Splash's README ships the launcher and names its Anthropic Messages endpoint; it never names Claude Code). Acceptance: one S item from the backlog done end to end on the Studio with a clean done report and a review by the other model; the driver's budget stop tested with a brief that cannot finish. Out of scope: anything the record keeps on the subscription (design, verdicts, diagnosis, cross-subsystem items, the first review of a safety change). Exit: `bash scripts/check.sh` and the done report. **Owner direction 2026-10-18 (harness and model order, from web research that was anecdotal, not benched):** the Studio has 128 GB, so Reika (chosen for the 24 GB laptop and small models) is not the default here; people on large-memory Macs mostly run OpenCode or Aider, and Cline in VS Code. Try Aider first (lightest, diff-based, git-native, fine at 16K context), on Qwen3.8-27B, then Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (about 125B total, 6B active, roughly 63 GB at 4-bit; vendor DeepSWE 58.7 against 42.2 for the 27B, a tie on SWE-bench Pro; independent index and one hands-on test favour the 27B, so measure it), then OpenCode on the winner, Reika last. Flash-Next is not yet a MEASURE-02 candidate; add it there. Every run goes through the LOCALCODER-SANDBOX-01 sandbox. **Pilot 2026-10-18 (this Mac, not through the Stack): Aider 0.86.2 on Splash 1.3.2 serving Qwen3.8-27B UD-Q4_K_M, thinking capped at medium effort and 2000 tokens, one S item (STATUS-APPS-REG-01) in its own worktree, 25-minute cap, the test as the only feedback loop.** Three attempts. Attempts one and two failed on the harness, not the model: `--yes-always` auto-adds any file the instruction names, and naming the 37,000-line `docs/dev.md` overflowed the context window both times (the first attempt also added it explicitly). Attempt three, with big files kept out of the instruction and the docs note written to a small new file, finished in 83 seconds (9.8k tokens sent, 5.6k received) and the test file passed 21 of 21, but the new test was vacuous: it hard-coded the list of shell destinations inside the test instead of reading the real navigation, so a new destination could never fail it, and the reasons it wrote for its allowlist were invented. Two causes: the item's own pointer was wrong (the backend cannot import `@maipai/ui`; the test belongs in the frontend beside `frontend/src/shell/statusApps.ts`), and the only feedback loop was 'tests pass', which a trivial test satisfies. Nothing landed. **Lessons the lane must build in:** pick items whose pointers a person has just verified; give every item an acceptance check that proves the new test can fail (plant a destination and watch it fail); never combine `--yes-always` with free-text file names or files over a few hundred lines; keep the instruction's named files small and add the rest by hand; a review by a different model is part of the lane, not optional; and the cheap parts worked: no Codex or Claude usage, 83 seconds per attempt, clean worktree discipline. The diff is kept in the session scratchpad (`pilot/pilot-attempt3.diff`).
    Design: [studio-day-one-2026-09-23](plans/studio-day-one-2026-09-23.md)
- [ ] **STUDIO-MOVE-01: the Studio beside this Mac, then the move, then the rollback** (S, Sonnet). Objective: this Mac's Home points its chat, embed and judge roles at the Studio's engines with the Studio as the household's engine computer (REMOTE-STACK-01): the whole Stack on the Studio, Home linked to it, the privacy page's engine computer rows; then Home moves per the runbook's step 11 with the Studio restoring from this Mac's last backup and this Mac's hub stopped, never deleted; rollback is repointing the URLs or restarting this Mac's hub on its untouched data directory. Acceptance: a turn on this Mac's hub answered by the Studio's engine; the rollback rehearsed. Exit: `bash scripts/check.sh --docs` and the recorded rehearsal.
    Design: [studio-day-one-2026-09-23](plans/studio-day-one-2026-09-23.md)

## Thin chat path

- [x] **MEMORY-MERGE-01: the judge merges two unrelated facts into one record** (S, 2026-10-17; live on the Studio, Qwen3 4B judge, nomic embed; rule 12). Repro: Bruno says "actually my favorite color is blue, not green" (a `remember` tool write), then in a new chat "Serena is my wife": the judge's dedupe answered SUPERSEDE with contradiction:false and merged_text "Bruno's favorite color is blue and Serena is Bruno's wife", retiring the colour record. Cause: `decideDedupe()` (`backend/src/lib/memoryJudge.ts`) accepts any merged_text in the 0.60 to 0.92 cosine band; measured on the live embed model, unrelated pairs that share a name score 0.62 to 0.76 and genuine refine or extend pairs 0.77 to 0.94, so no cosine floor separates them. Decide between a dedupe prompt that forbids joining two facts about different things (measured on a fixture set) and a structural check (a merge must keep one subject). Regression test first. Exit: `bash scripts/check.sh --pre` plus `backend/tests/memoryJudge.test.ts`. Landed 2026-10-17: a merge that keeps the old fact true must share a non-name word with it (`sharesAttribute`), a correction keeps the person's own words, and the dedupe prompt forbids joining different things. Live check: correction retired green, the wife fact stayed its own record; recall not judged (Stack restarting).
- [x] **WHO-ASK-02: the who-question fires on a name whose kind the sentence states, and follows the person into unrelated chats** (S, 2026-10-17; live; ASK-01). "actually my dog's name is Rivet, not Rover" got "Who's Rivet?"; the same question was appended to "what's my shoe size?" in a new chat minutes later. Decide: a sentence that names the kind ("my dog's name is X") answers its own who-question; a pending question is asked once more at most, in the chat it came from. Exit: `bash scripts/check.sh --pre` plus `backend/tests/askNames*.test.ts`. Landed 2026-10-17: "my dog's name is X" / "is named X" frames the kind (no question); a queued question not in play is asked only in the chat it came from.
- [ ] **CHAT-CLOCK-01: the date and time stop opening chat replies** (S, 2026-10-10; bug from the live hub; rules 1, 2 and 3; the model decides, no word rule, no output rewriting; model floor Sonnet 5.5; diagnosis `data-scratch/design/CHAT-DATE-PHOTOS-DIAGNOSIS-2026-10-10.md`, part A). Objective: a 9B model parroted "The current time is Saturday, October 10, 2026 at 2:45 AM." as its first sentence, then replayed it from history as a few-shot example. Cause: the "clock" context item (`backend/src/lib/turnMachine/nodes/context.ts:338-342`) is rendered as an unlabelled "Clock:" section of the final user message directly above the person's words (`backend/src/lib/turnMachine/messages.ts:186,231,236`, moved there by 8084b3f6). Change the framing, not the content: label it as reference data to mention only if the person asks or the answer depends on it, and move it away from the person's words; best cache behaviour is a day-granular date with no time of day in the stable prefix, refreshed daily (a minute-level value breaks the prompt cache). Do not add a regex that strips date openers from replies. Acceptance: on the CHAT-AB-01 fresh set the 9B no longer opens unrelated replies with the date or time, and "what time is it" and "what day is it" still answer correctly (tool-decision and recall, rule 3); the stable-prefix cache hit is not worse (cache_n on a second turn equals the prior prompt prefix); a regression test pins the clock item's wording and position. Reuse check: edits the existing clock item and its rendering only. Exit: `bash scripts/check.sh`.

Objective: when a stored turn has an `image_gallery` block, the history window builder shows it as a native `show_images` tool call plus tool result (the engine's own feature) instead of leaving "Photos of ... are on your screen" as bare assistant prose, so a small model sees "call the tool, get a result" as the pattern for pictures and stops copying the claim sentence. Evidence: in conv-aei9cpo012 turn 1 called `show_images` and stored a gallery; on turns 2 and 3 the 9B skipped the tool and claimed "The photos ... are on your screen" with an invented description. Files: the history window builder, `backend/src/lib/turnMachine/nodes/tool.ts:76-80,124-132` (call and result line, which says not to describe the pictures), `backend/packages/show_images/manifest.json`. Acceptance: a replayed turn with a gallery renders as a call and result pair with the same result line a live call produces; a turn without a gallery is unchanged; a follow-up "show me" on the CHAT-AB-01 fresh set calls `show_images` at least as often as before (measured, 9B and the catalog 27B); a regression test builds the window from a stored gallery turn. Reuse check: reuses the live tool-result line builder, no second copy. Exit: `bash scripts/check.sh`.
- [ ] **CHAT-FALSE-CLAIM-01: one stable-prompt line against false claims of a lookup or pictures** (S, 2026-10-10; rules 1, 3 and 6; model floor Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5 only if the bench is contradictory; diagnosis `data-scratch/design/CHAT-DATE-PHOTOS-DIAGNOSIS-2026-10-10.md`, part B fixes 2 and 3). Objective: a turn with no tool outcome must not say it searched, checked the web or showed pictures. Evidence: turn 2 said "I've checked the web ... reading the top pages now" with no search run, and turn 3 said photos were on screen with none shown (`outcomes` and `blocks` empty). Fix: add one sentence to the stable prompt for adult written turns that a lookup or pictures exist only when a tool result says so. No word rule and no output matching; a typed grounding check on the output gate is allowed only if it needs no wording match, otherwise skipped. Bench before adopting (rule 3): run the CHAT-AB-01 fresh set with `show_images` follow-ups ("show me", "what does he look like") on the 9B and the catalog 27B, with and without the line, and record false-claim rate and tool-call rate. If the 9B still skips the tool, that is a model-record finding (rule 8), not a pipeline fix. Acceptance: bench numbers with engine build, model file and sanitized hardware in the report; the line is adopted only if the false-claim rate drops and the tool-call and answer-quality sets do not regress; a regression test pins the line's presence. Reuse check: one sentence in the existing stable prompt, no new node. Exit: `bash scripts/check.sh`.

- [ ] **GATE-FAST-01: the gate is faster, lighter and does not flake** (M, measurement first; owner asked 2026-10-07 after a day in which most landings needed two or three gate runs). Evidence from 2026-10-06 and 07, to be confirmed by stage timing, not trusted: (a) full gates take 25 to 35 minutes under load and any pin bump, package.json, lockfile or scripts change forces the full scope; (b) most red gates were cheap deterministic failures found late (stale `elements-adoption.json`, `docs/api` drift, lint baselines, an unstaged generated file, a pin worktree in the wrong place) after many minutes of tests; (c) flakes outside the diff: chatTurn FOREIGN KEY, UsersPage roster fetch, sidecars decoy port, memoryJudge timeout, chatFolderProjects clock ordering, a11y ECONNRESET to the throwaway backend, backend shard 6 'AI was stopped' (a test that reaches a live engine path); (d) a lane once queued 29 gates at once and held the machine at load 40; (e) the gate's test workers hold several GB, which competes with the chat engine on the 24 GB laptop; (f) each fresh worktree runs `bun install --force` twice. Levers to evaluate in this order, each measured before and after, none weakening a check: 1. **fail fast**: run the cheap deterministic checks (generated files fresh, adoption scan, api docs, UI-rules lint, typecheck) before the lock and before any long test, as `check.sh --pre`, so a red costs about a minute; 2. **hermetic tests**: no test may touch the live Stack, a fixed port, the live hub db or the real clock (inject the clock like GATE-FIX-03; ports via reserveFreePort; one scratch db per file); a lint that fails a test importing the live Stack URL; 3. **flake ledger with teeth**: scripts/gate/flakes.json entries get an owner and a deadline, the gate reruns ONLY a listed test once and records it, an unlisted failure is a real failure; 4. **content-addressed skipping**: extend the existing 'a11y skipped because its inputs are unchanged' idea to backend and frontend test shards keyed by the hash of the files and dependencies they import. Pin-only scope is owner-approved as a separate org rule change, not part of this lever; 5. **machine limits**: cap shard workers by available memory so the gate cannot starve the chat engine, one gate per worktree, one waiter per lane, no polling loops (a lock queue); 6. **install cost**: use one root `bun install --frozen-lockfile`, forcing only on a pin change. Do not clone `node_modules`; this is the 01f approach. Step 0: instrument stage times and failure reasons for 20 gate runs (the logs under data-scratch/chat-ab/queue/logs and the gate's own output) and report the top offenders before changing anything. Architect gate before dispatch (the gate is a rule-bearing path); review medium.

## Chat throughput (owner, 2026-10-17)

From `docs/design/chat-throughput-2026-10-17.md`: 25 tok/s is the bandwidth ceiling of a dense 30B on this chip (31.2 ceiling, 26.1 measured); flags are not the cause.

Objective: llama-bench halved to about 14 tok/s twice while chat and other work shared the GPU. Run `llama-bench -p 0 -n 64` against a scratch copy while the judge and embed roles generate and while a chat streams, record tok/s alone vs shared, and log `predicted_per_second` next to which roles were busy. If shared halves it, the fix is scheduling (prewarm and judge work wait for an idle chat), a separate row. Done when: a table of alone vs shared numbers lands in the design note.
    Design: [chat-throughput-2026-10-17](design/chat-throughput-2026-10-17.md)

Temperature 0 outputs diverge after 40 to 170 tokens on 4 of 5 prompts, so the gate is the quality benches, not string equality. Draft: `dflash-Muse-Glimmer-30B-Q4_K_M.gguf` from `meta-models/Muse-Glimmer-30B-GGUF` revision `70bf1b61ac09f91b24d39038091b41c582bc5d7a`, 1,631,208,128 bytes, sha256 `b2e808bf656086fe86bd0d0bd990f01d33e377537a07c02d45371517c8b264ef` (verified). **Quality benches run (3 seeds each, draft vs none):** tool calling 128/174 against 129/174 correct, 0 corpus false calls both, reasoning 60/60 both, search decision 15/24 against 17/24 on 8 rows (noise); quality holds. **Combined with the projector (tested 2026-10-17): no gain.** Draft plus projector in one launch starts and engages (46 to 49% acceptance) but runs at 21 to 24 tok/s against 26 without the draft; the same draft without the projector gives 30 to 35. You want a quick rundown ...?" and never a list; the reply was also flat where the companion should open with a reaction). Cause found: the spoken plan for that turn was `max_sentences 2, max_words 30, react required`; the short length rule reads as a reason to decline a "name every" request. Measured with `scripts/bench/datasets/spoken-list-01.json` (10 list requests, 5 statements a lively companion should react to; `chat-ab-01.ts --group spoken` with `MAIPAI_AB_SPOKEN_PROMPTS`, summarized by `summarizeSpokenList.py`) on the live Qwen3.6, default companion, 3 runs: 22 of 30 list requests answered with a real list. A plan-line sentence ("name the main ones in one go within those sentences and offer more; never say you cannot or ask permission first") was tried and gave 23 of 30, no change, so it was not shipped. The companion voice does reach the model (the composed prompt carries the lively examples; the default companion opens with a reaction in 10 of 15 statements); the flat robot reply is not explained by a missing prompt, and the bench does not run the robot surface or the rivet companion, so the exact live pair is not reproduced. Options for the owner (rule 0 says nothing changes how a spoken turn is shaped): (a) when the evidence says the answer is a list (`evidence.choices >= 2` or `deliverable`), the spoken cap rises from 30 words to about 60 for that turn; (b) accept it; (c) a robot-surface bench with the rivet companion to measure before choosing.
- [x] **ROBOT-VOICE-01: the robot sounds like its companion, and brings back what it was told** (S, 2026-10-21; rules 0, 13 and 14; live on the robot, Qwen3.6: replies like "Got it. What's next?" where default StackChan is energetic and friendly, and no follow-up on a remembered fact, e.g. "I'm making a slushy" then, ten turns later, "say hello to my wife"). Cause found, measured with `scripts/bench/robotVoice.ts` (the real spoken-class messages for the Rivet companion at adult controls, a window and a memory line, sent to the live Qwen3.6 with production sampling; 10 scenarios x 4 runs): the persona prefix does reach the model (companion section 1,424 of 1,500 characters, examples kept), but the plan line is the last thing the model reads and for a neutral statement it says "no required move" and "no unnecessary follow-up", which cancelled the companion's habit of reacting first and of bringing back earlier facts. Fix: (a) data, in the four bundled companions' `behavior` (Rivet, Nova, Riff, Sprout): "Start with a quick, happy reaction ... before anything else" and "When something they told you earlier fits what they say now, bring it back in a playful way" (the companion-package field DYNAMIC-COMPANION-01 made for this); (b) code, one sentence on a curious companion's spoken plan line: "If something you remember about them, or they said earlier, fits, tie it in playfully" (memory use, not voice). Before (production): warm opener 28/40, an exclamation 18/40, remembered-fact follow-up 2/8. After: warm opener 35 to 40 of 40, exclamation 29 to 31 of 40, follow-up 5 to 8 of 8 (two runs); Nova: 27/30, 17/30, 4/6. Plain answers stay plain ("Paris, duh."). Rule 14 reading: it forbids voice adapters being prompt prose; companion behavior lines are existing package data and the code sentence is about memory, so nothing was changed in the rule; the owner may veto the sentence. Not measured: the robot surface itself (a device, speaker evidence, the real signal classifier); the harness builds the same messages without them. Open: robot replies where the plan forbids a reaction (a backchannel, a closing) stay short by design; the Star-Spangled Banner refusal as "copyrighted" is a Qwen3.6 fact error (it is public domain), a separate item.
- [x] **ROBOT-VOICE-02: the real robot turn, replayed with the household's own history** (S, 2026-10-21; rules 0, 13 and 14; ROBOT-VOICE-01 measured well on a bench and did not work on the device: Home v0.2.91 still answered "Got it. What's next?", "You're right, I'm here and listening" and, for the national anthem and the Pledge, "I can't provide the full lyrics since they're copyrighted"). The bench had no history; the device's conversation is one long thread (a day of its own short replies), and the model copies it. Reproduced for real: `tests/robotRealBench.test.ts` (off unless `MAIPAI_REAL_CHAT` names a llama-server) copies a snapshot of the household database into a scratch one, replays the robot's real conversation and Rivet at adult controls, and keeps the full composed messages; its plan matched the stored plan of the three live turns exactly. Causes found on the real path: (1) the plan line for a directive or question read "say, one sentence, no question, no tasks" and react was forbidden, so a lively companion answered flat; (2) the companion section was cut at 1,500 characters (Rivet at adult is 1,616), losing its last examples; (3) "I said you're freaking out" was read as the speaker's fear, which forced care, no playfulness; (4) the model, given a 25 word cap, refused lists and recitals as "too long" or "copyrighted" (the anthem and the Pledge are public domain). Fix: a curious companion's spoken plan line now carries the voice (upbeat, a quick happy reaction first, bring back something said earlier) except where care leads; react is allowed for every act on that class; a feeling word after "you're/you seem" is not the speaker's; one rules sentence says public-domain texts are free to say; caps 950 (rules) and 1,700 (companion). Measured on the replayed real conversation, 24 turns x 3 runs: warm opener 49% to 88%, an exclamation 25% to 85%, flat openers 6% to 1%, copyright or cannot-list refusals 4% to 0%; "say hello to my wife" after a slushy 2 of 6 to 4 of 6 mention the slushy (the plan sentence reworded; the first wording was 2 of 6). The three live turns, replayed: "Let's break it out." and the Pledge are now said with a "Yay" or "Ooh"; "you're freaking out" is answered as about the robot. Not measured: a real device turn on the live hub (needs a Home tag); sampling varies run to run (one of nine replays invented a wrong Pledge line). Open: spoken replies still sometimes print markdown (bold, numbered lists) that a speaker would read aloud; an example line ("Ooh, you're cooking?") is sometimes copied for other topics.
- [x] **ROBOT-VOICE-03: the robot's callbacks are rare, relevant and faithful** (S, 2026-10-23; rules 13 and 14; Jesse on the live robot after ROBOT-VOICE-02: it keeps bringing up the same past thing and invents details around it, e.g. "Bianca and her bee-mode robot" for what was the StackChan itself). Found by replaying the robot's real conversation with the household's rows (`tests/robotRealBench.test.ts`): the tie-in sentence ROBOT-VOICE-02 put on every spoken turn, plus the always-on persona line, plus the window of the robot's own earlier replies that already mentioned Bianca, made it repeat the callback on short replies ("Are you there?", "Thank you.") and embroider it. Fix (one sentence in `register.ts`): the tie-in is offered only on a turn that says something (a statement, a plan or a request, by the turn signal's own act), not on a question, greeting, thanks or goodbye; and it now says to use only what they said, add no details, never turn something about the robot into something about a person, not to bring up anything mentioned in the last few replies, and that most replies bring nothing back. Measured on the replay (8 turns x 3 to 4 runs): replies that mention Bianca or the bee-mode 8 of 24 (33%) before, 2 of 32 (6%) after, both on a turn that really refers to her ("No, she is not"); the slushy then "say hello to my wife" case mentions the slushy 4 of 8 after (4 of 6 before). Tried and dropped: removing the persona line (Bianca 0 of 32 but slushy 1 of 8), a stronger "clearly connects" wording (slushy 1 of 8, 0 of 4), and an embedding gate (nomic similarity does not separate related from unrelated short turns: 0.56 to 0.67 for related pairs, 0.47 to 0.71 for unrelated). Not fixed: the window itself still carries what was said; a separate model call to pick a relevant earlier statement would be the next step and costs a call per robot turn. Open: the memory "Jesse is talking to Bianca, Jesse's daughter" is a moment, not a fact, and was stored as a durable memory.
- [x] **WEATHER-ASSIST-01: a small learned detector rescues a weather question the model answered without the weather tool** (M, 2026-10-21; rule 1's scoped weather exception, owner-approved in chat; follows RECENCY-02). Built: `scripts/train/weatherHead.ts` trains a binary linear head on the nomic embedding Home already makes (`src/lib/searchAssist/weather-head.json`, bundled, nothing downloaded; 363 labelled sentences in 32 families, leave-families-out: 93.3% precision, 85.7% recall at the recorded threshold 0.568), `searchAssist/weatherAssist.ts` scores each eligible turn (tool offered, household home set, a turn that offers tools) and records `weather_assist` beside `search_assist` on the turn's stats; with `chat.search_assist` = rescue the model node holds a plain-text first round on an over turn and, if the model made no call, a one-line place writer reads a named place (none means the household home) and the weather tool is called; the model phrases the result. Works on spoken turns, for an unidentified speaker and for every age band; the band's output gate is unchanged; off and shadow never hold. Counters `weather_scored`, `weather_over_threshold`, `weather_rescued`, `weather_rescued_at_budget`. Measured on the live Qwen3.6 through the real turn path, 24 weather phrasings that are not in the training corpus x3 plus 12 that must not call weather x3, a household home set: model alone 53/72 (73%); with the rescue 72/72 (100%, 11 rescued); false rescues 3 of 36, all "she's under the weather today" (an idiom; its near twins are in the corpus now, so that item is no longer held out). Open: the corpus is small and written by one author, so a second labelled set from real turns (the weather prompts people actually speak) should replace it; a corpus-driven threshold moved between 0.56 and 0.71 as 14 sentences were added, so re-measure after any corpus change; the same head design for other tools (a calendar or timer head) is one more class and threshold in a manifest, not an engine.

The live hub's database is root-owned and `PUT /api/settings` takes only a signed-in browser session, so a session could not flip `chat.search_assist`. Built: commons `spec-v0.1.204` adds the `settings` scope to `api-key`; Home pins it (installer digests included). `apiKeys.ts`: a settings key is made only by an owner or admin who is still enabled, stands alone (no other scope), lasts 7, 30 or 90 days, is checked again on every call (a demoted or removed holder loses it at once and the key reads as suspended), and is stored peppered-hashed, shown once, revocable, never logged (docs/CREDENTIALS.md). `lib/operatorSettings.ts` holds the allowlist (today only `chat.search_assist`; a test fails if a key from a denied family such as people, auth, safety, age, credentials, privacy, retention, generation, kids, backups, network, the Stack address or robots is ever added). `routes/operator.ts`: `GET /api/operator/settings` lists the allowed settings with their values and options, `PUT /api/operator/settings {key, value}` writes through the same writer the Settings page uses and logs the key id, the setting and the two values; bearer only, no cookie fallback, one refusal for a missing, wrong, expired, revoked or wrong-scope key. - [ ] **CHAT-TYPEAHEAD-01: warm the engine's prompt cache while a person types or speaks, so the first word after Send comes sooner** (M, Home and Stack; idea 2026-10-22, from the mafdet prototype `TheLastOxygen/mafdet`, Apache-2.0, Windows and NVIDIA only). Needs a design note and an architect verdict before any code; not pickup-ready. Objective: after a typing pause (about 500 to 800 ms, tuned by measurement), send the stable prompt prefix plus the draft to the local chat engine as a cache-fill request (no tokens generated) so only the changed tail is read on Send. Prefix-only: the engine reuses the longest common token prefix, so the result is identical to a cold run and nothing speculative can be wrong. Measure first: time from Send to first visible word with and without the warm-up on the Studio, and how much of that time is reading the prompt (the 2026-10-21 table above gives 164 to 564 pieces/s). If reading the prompt is under about 300 ms on the usual turn, stop and record that. Design questions for the note: (1) put per-turn text last so the system, memory and history prefix stays byte-stable; (2) whether the Stack's engine and its slot handling keep the cache across requests and across a model switch (MODEL-SWITCH-01); (3) priority: chat first, then images, then video, so a warm-up yields at once to any real turn and never queues behind or ahead of one; (4) the draft goes only to the local engine and passes the same age, surface and temporary-mode gates as a sent message, is never logged, stored, searched or given to a tool, and is dropped on clear, Incognito or leaving the composer; (5) the voice path, where the same warm-up could run on a partial transcript; (6) a setting, default off until measured, with no new status UI (reuse the existing ones). Out of scope: reasoning ahead of Send and writing an answer ahead (not exact, and any edit discards them), intent prediction, prefetching searches or any tool call, anything that writes. Reuse check: the engine's own prompt cache (llama-server prompt caching and slots) is the implementation; mafdet is a reference for the approach only (nothing is vendored); no hand-built cache. Exit: the measurement table in the design note, then `bash scripts/check.sh` per the slice.
    Design: not written yet (`docs/design/chat-typeahead-2026-10-22.md`, to be created by the design pass)

The fix is two prompt edits, no forcing and no word rule: the date line (`datesText`) adds that training is months behind, that an unrecognized recent event is more likely missing than untrue, and that a claim about something recent is searched before it is denied; the `show_images` subject description adds that "show me" a picture or poster uses it instead of a web search. Measured (runs of 2; searched / needed): Qwen3.6 before 16/28 recency, 3/4 weather, 6/8 show-me with show_images, 4/20 false searches; after 26/28, 4/4, 6/8 (1 web search, 0 none), 1/20.     Status 2026-10-21: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (Unsloth UD-Q4_K_XL, 22.4 GB, plus its 0.9 GB picture file) is pinned in the Stack and Home, installable and choosable in Settings, Models (MODEL-SWITCH-01); Muse stays the default (STACK-MUSE-01).     | | Muse Glimmer 30B | Qwen3.6-35B-A3B |
    |---|---|---|
    | Voice: first visible word | 4.2 s (hidden reasoning runs first) | 0.22 s |
    | Voice: whole reply | 4.9 s | 0.7 s |
    | Voice: tokens per reply | 104 (about 80 of them reasoning) | 24 |
    | Written: first visible word | 2.8 s | 0.16 s |
    | Written: 946 vs 1,305 tokens | 41 s | 18 s |
    | Decode speed | 23 pieces/s | 74 pieces/s (peaks 80) |
    | Reading the prompt | 164 to 200 pieces/s | 336 to 564 pieces/s |
    The robot's 4 to 9 s replies were hidden reasoning: Muse spent about 80 tokens thinking before every 20-token answer, and Qwen3.6 with `enable_thinking` false spends none. Checked on the real chat template (`/apply-template`): the system line and the date reach the model and the tools render, a tool call comes back parsed (a timer, a search for last night's game, none for the capital of France), but the template silently drops a system message that comes after the first user message; Home's `foldLateSystemMessages` (CHAT-LATE-SYSTEM-01) already merges those into the first, so nothing is lost through Home, and any new caller must go through `chatRequestBody`. A small direct tool check (two tools, five needing one, five not, five repeats each, thinking off) gave 25 of 25 tool calls and 0 of 25 false calls for both Qwen3.6 and Muse. Not yet run: CHAT-AB-01 fresh-search and the full tool bench on this model (the harness refuses beside another session's running gate; rerun `bun run scripts/bench/chat-ab-01.ts --group fresh` against a Stack with Qwen3.6 chosen), MODEL-VET-01, and a long-context quality check. Home's sampling adds min_p, XTC and DRY beside the card's presence_penalty 1.5; that mix is unmeasured on this model. The decision stays Jesse's.

## The chat rebuild (2026-09-22)

The accepted design and build order:
[docs/plans/simple-turn-pipeline-2026-09-22.md](plans/simple-turn-pipeline-2026-09-22.md).
The old rule ladder (~1,900 lines of regex and word lists deciding
whether to search, what to search for, and whether to trust the model's
own answer) is replaced by five fixed steps and one model call with
tools; new path built beside the old one behind `turn.pipeline.next`
(off by default) until the replay set passes clean. Phase 0 (the
buy-or-build spike, the per-model capability numbers, the local-decider
bench) gates U2 onward; U0, U1, U3, U5 start immediately. See the plan's
point 7 for the full unit list and point 6 for the migration order.

- [ ] **JUDGE-SURFACE-01: personaJudge.ts always judges a written reply against the spoken persona description** (S; found live during U4b-2's own voice A/B, 2026-09-23). Objective: `personaJudge.ts`'s `buildJudgePrompt` calls `composePersonaPrompt(persona)` with no surface class argument, defaulting to "spoken", so a written-class exchange is always graded against the spoken description ("use contractions", "not like a written page") - a structured written reply reads as "does not match the persona" for that reason alone, regardless of whether it is actually voiced correctly for its own register. Confirmed live: three written exchanges scored 0/3 both with and without the few-shot examples block, an indistinguishable result caused by the mismatch, not a real signal either way. Change: `judgePersonaConsistency` and `buildJudgePrompt` take a `surfaceClass` parameter, passed through to `composePersonaPrompt`, defaulting to "spoken" so `persona-eval.ts`'s existing spoken-only call site needs no edit. Files: `personaJudge.ts`, `personaJudge.test.ts`. Tests in these words: `buildJudgePrompt(persona, exchanges, "written")`'s own prompt contains the written formality fragment, not the spoken one. Acceptance: a written exchange scored against the written description instead of the spoken one. Exit: `bash scripts/check.sh`.
- [ ] **ROUTER-FOLLOWUP-01: close the dev-versus-lock-box gap** (M). Dev recall was 89 to 99.7% and the sealed lock box gave 75 to 86%, so the dev pool and labels are easier than real turns. Find why (family leakage, label noise, phrasing mix), then refit the head on a pool that predicts the lock box.
    Design: [router-build-02-2026-10-12](plans/router-build-02-2026-10-12.md)
- [ ] **SEARCH-DDGS-01b: spec copy for the ddgs option** (S). In commons `spec/settings/keys.json` change `search.web_sources` help and `copy.options.ddgs` from "not available yet" to true copy (a second, adults-only source; needs the search service on this computer), tag, then bump the pin in Home.
- [ ] **SEARCH-DDGS-01c: persist the ddgs quiet window across hub restarts** (S). It is in memory today; needs a household-scoped state record declared in the spec first.

## Chat freshness (owner, 2026-10-07)

- [ ] **SEARCH-FRESH-01: the model searches by itself for anything current instead of answering from stale memory, and never asks permission to search** (M, bug from the live hub 2026-10-07; rules 1, 7 and 13; the model decides, no word rule or router). Owner transcript: "when is the new movie coming out" (about The Exorcist) was answered from training memory as "Believer, May 24, 2023" with "as of September 2024" and an offer "Would you like me to check?"; "nope, theres a newer one" got another stale answer; only after the person typed "yes" did it search and find the real answer (The Exorcist: Martyrs, 12 March 2027). Two defects: (1) a question about something new, latest, upcoming or current was answered without the search tool; the model also believes the date is September 2024, so the clock line is missing, buried or ignored; (2) it asked permission to search instead of searching. Acceptance by measurement, not by word lists: a fixed set of at least 30 time-sensitive questions (new movie, latest version, who is the current ..., upcoming release, today's score, price now) and 30 timeless ones (arithmetic, capital cities, definitions) run on the live model through the existing search bench (THIN-AB / chat-ab-01): time-sensitive questions call the search tool in at least 90% of runs and never end by asking whether to search; timeless questions do not search more often than today (no new unnecessary searches); the answer states the date it relies on only when sourced. Levers allowed (each measured before and after, in the owner's order of preference): the date and year given to the model in a place it uses (system prompt top, not a buried line), the search tool's description (when to use it, plain words, no keyword list), the instruction that a search is never to be offered, only done. Architect verdict first (Chat turn rules govern); review medium.

## Tool offering (owner, 2026-10-07)

- [~] **TOOL-OFFER-01: a tool can never silently go missing from what the model is offered** (S to M, owner question after the show_images bug: the tool was installed, enabled and gate-approved but absent from both models' hand-written `turn_budget.tools_offered` lists in `backend/src/lib/modelCatalog.ts`, so the model never saw it; nothing failed, the model just said it could not show pictures). Three layers, strongest first. (1) **Inventory:** every bundled tool must be in the derived offer or have a visible reason why it is not offered. (2) **One definition (principle 4):** package manifests declare base, conditional or off; the live `tools_offered` set is derived from installed, enabled, smoke-healthy manifests plus the model's `max_tools` cap, and over-cap fails closed rather than silently trimming. (3) **An offer test per tool:** representative prompts by allowed mode, real adult written request assertion, per-tool call-rate bench, and a model-vetter parseable-call check. Architect verdict approved; spec offer block is present in spec-v0.1.108. STATUS 2026-10-08: layers (1) and (2) implemented; layer (3) remains open.

- [ ] **CHAT-STATUS-ONE-01: the rail Chat LED and tooltip, the line under the chat input and the profile status say the same thing** (S to M; owner bug 2026-10-08). Same state, same colour, same meaning on all three (one can be wordier, never different): one function maps availability to colour key, label and long copy.
- [ ] **CHAT-MENU-01: the per-chat context menu (the three dots in the chat header) matches ChatGPT in options and look** (S to M; owner 2026-10-07; screenshots chatgpt-chat-menu.png and ours-chat-menu.png). Ours has Rename, Read replies aloud and Delete only, drawn small and tight. ChatGPT's: Rename, Pin, then a divider and View files in chat, then Archive and Delete (red), then a project group: Move to project (submenu) and Remove from project when the chat is in one. Scope: Rename, Pin or Unpin, Archive or Unarchive, Delete (confirm dialog), Move to project (submenu of the person's projects, projects landed in PROJECTS-P1/P2 and UI), Remove from project, View files in this chat only if the chat has attachments, Read replies aloud kept (it is ours: the read-aloud Element). Each item uses an existing backend route where one exists (list which are missing: archive, move, remove are the likely gaps) with a spec-first record change if needed; no item is shown that does nothing; a child sees only what their rules allow (Incognito and temporary chats: no pin, archive or project). Look: the kit dropdown menu part as it ships, a roomy row height (about 40 px, 18 px icons), group dividers, destructive in the danger token, a Share button beside it only if sharing exists. Kit and shadcn parts only, tokens only. Architect verdict first.

## Model vetting (owner, 2026-10-07)

- [ ] **MODEL-VET-01 (design note: data-scratch/design/MODEL-VETTING-DESIGN.md, owner answers 2026-10-07 in OWNER-ANSWERS.md; eight slices, spec first; the seed list below is superseded by the design note): a model vetter: a new or changed model answers a fixed set of simple questions, and a model that gets them wrong is not loaded** (M, owner idea 2026-10-07 after a live failure: the Qwen3-VL chat template silently dropped every later system message, so memory, the clock and the age instructions never reached the model, and nothing noticed for hours; found only because the owner asked "why is the date wrong"). The Stack's chat role row already carries a `check` field (state "not checked", reason, at, stale) and the picture check (the engine loads its projector and reads a check picture before it declares `imageInput`): this item generalises that into one vetting suite. Candidate checks, all deterministic with exact expected answers, never a judge model in the safety path (RULES-AND-LEARNED-COMPONENTS.md): (1) **context reaches the model**: a fact and a date placed the way Home places them (the exact message layout Home sends) must be answered back; this is the check that would have caught the template bug, and it must run through the real template (llama-server /apply-template or a real completion), not a unit stub; (2) arithmetic and a short instruction ("reply with exactly: ready"); (3) tool-call syntax: given a toy tool the model emits a parseable call when it should and none when it should not; (4) thinking off honoured when the request says off; (5) picture check for a vision model (already exists); (6) context recall near the configured window (a fact at the start recovered at 80% fill); (7) a held-back-at-this-age line followed for a child persona (exact phrasing check on a fixed prompt, counted only as pass or fail, never used to loosen anything). Where it runs: in the Stack, after the engine process is up and before the role is marked ready; a failing model leaves the role offline with a plain-words reason for admins ("the model did not pass check N"), is never loaded for a household, and the previous good model stays; the result is stored per model file hash and per template hash so a re-download or a template change re-vets it; new models install from the catalog but stay "not vetted" until they pass. Design note first: the check list with expected answers, the pass bar (all of 1 to 5 required, 6 and 7 per role), cost in seconds on the 24 GB machine, the admin view on the Models page (kit parts only), and how Home's own prompt layout is fed to check 1 without Stack importing Home (the layout is declared once in `commons` spec so both read the same shape). Spec first, Stack, then Home. Architect gate before dispatch (Stack rules and the safety path); no learned component in the safety path.
    Design: [chat-engine-and-model-records-2026-10-17](design/chat-engine-and-model-records-2026-10-17.md)

## Knowledge sources (2026-09-24)

- [ ] **MEDIA-SEARCH-01: video, approved 2026-09-24** **Amended 2026-10-06 by ANSWER-IMG-02: video only; pictures in answers are the ANSWER-IMG items, so two items never cover pictures.** **Rewritten 2026-10-02 for chat rule 7.** Depends on THIN-4A (page-reading search) as well as LOOKUP-FED-01. The picture and video card is a tool the model chooses; IMAGE-SEARCH-01 is dropped and merged here. For a child or teen the results pass the same deterministic floor as page text (THIN-4C). (S, after `LOOKUP-FED-01`; merges `IMAGE-SEARCH-01`). Objective: `docs/plans/knowledge-sources-2026-09-24.md`'s "Video search" section. Results come from SearXNG's images/videos categories through the one `lookup()`, its limiter and its cache - the hub never downloads a video. Card: a thumbnail through Home's own image proxy, title, site, length and date; tapping plays on the viewer's own device (the site's privacy-enhanced embed or its page), never routed through the hub. A child or teen only ever gets `SEARCH-SAFE-01`'s own safe-search-capable engines, so no YouTube in results unless an adult allows it for that person. How a turn asks for media (the lookup returning media rows with the card shown vs. one dedicated "find media" tool) is decided by measurement on replay rows ("show me the trailer" vs. "who directed it"), the same discipline `#150`/`READ-PAGE-01` already use. `YOUTUBE-API-01` (optional, off by default, the household's own key) comes after this ships. Exit: the replay bench table in dev.md, then `bash scripts/check.sh`.

## Reverse image lookup (owner, 2026-10-07)

- [ ] **IMG-REVERSE-01: "where is this picture from / what is this?" for a picture a person gives chat** (S design note first, then M, owner asked 2026-10-07 "dont know if thats possible"; part of the media work beside MEDIA-SEARCH-01 and the ANSWER-IMG items). Two different jobs, kept apart: (A) **local, private, buildable now**: the vision model already says what a picture shows (VISION-02 landed); add "find my pictures like this one" over the household's own photos by a local embedding or perceptual hash index (nothing leaves the home, per person and per age band like every media record, never another person's private photos). (B) **real reverse image search on the open web** (where else does this picture appear, who made it): no free official API exists (Google Lens and Bing Visual Search are not public APIs; TinEye has a paid API; the open-source SearXNG instance we run has image engines for text queries, not for uploading a picture). It would send the person's picture to a third party, which collides with the privacy architecture (docs/PRIVACY.md: nothing leaves the home, no outbound connection added without the owner's word) and THIRD-PARTY-SERVICES.md (a person's pace, the front door). So B needs the owner's decision (an owner-keyed optional provider, off by default, never for a child or teen, picture sent only after an adult taps a plain-words confirmation, EXIF location stripped) and an architect verdict; it is not built until then. Design note first: what is feasible, the provider options with their terms and cost, the consent card wording, and the local index size on a 24 GB machine. Architect gate before dispatch; no build in this item until the note is approved.
    Design: [chat-engine-and-model-records-2026-10-17](design/chat-engine-and-model-records-2026-10-17.md)

## Vision

- [ ] **Pet recognition: name a pet, mark its owner, recognize it again**
      (L, Jesse's ask, 2026-09-06) - "facial"/body recognition from an
      image plus, ideally, bark/vocalization recognition from audio.
      Blocked on the same missing image-input path as `host.camera.still`
      above (no pipeline exists to get a photo INTO the hub at all yet),
      and bark/sound recognition is a real second model, not a
      by-product of the vision half. Ownership is not new scope to
      invent: "pets need ownership" is one of Jesse's own original
      points in `docs/dev.md`'s "Entities, relationships and grants" -
      a pet is a `kind: entity` record and "owns"/"belongs to" is exactly
      the Relationship edge that spec already defines. That storage is
      real now (Session F step 7, 2026-09-06: `POST /api/entities`
      `kind: pet`, `POST /api/relationships` `type: owns` - its stored
      inverse, `owned_by`, comes free), so this is purely a recognition-
      and-UI problem sitting on top of already-built hub work, not a new
      data model to design from scratch.

## Voices (owner, 2026-10-17; queued after music)

From [voices-2026-10-18.md](design/voices-2026-10-18.md): Jesse asked for more than the Default voice and for admins to add more. Chatterbox Turbo takes a reference clip (more than 5 s) but the Stack ignores `voice_url` today; a starter set comes from CC0 donated voices and synthetic Kokoro clips. Owner rulings 2026-10-18: "Only admins can create voices" (owner and admin only; everyone picks, a child or teen from a curated subset) and "Admin can create a voice with whatever they want, no limitations" (any clip, no consent step, attestation, confirmation or content check). Kept, none a limit on creation: the text floors on what a voice says, an audit line, one plain sentence on the create screen, provenance on saved speech. Not started until MUSIC-GEN-06 is done.

- [ ] **VOICES-01: honest list, one gate and the role rule** (S, Stack `speech/voiceList.ts`, `routes/voices.ts`; Home `VoiceBrowserSection.tsx`, `routes/voice.ts`). Standard replaces "Chatterbox default"; the four named LibriVox Pocket presets (Bill Boerst, Caro Davy, Peter Yearsley, Stuart Bell) are hidden; options grouped; the child refusal becomes an `audience` flag; the preview cache keys on any voice id; add, upload and pack-install routes are owner and admin only (403 for member, teen, child) while everyone picks.
- [ ] **VOICES-02: the starter voices** (L; **built 2026-10-20, the clip-voice part only** (design `docs/design/household-voices-2026-10-20.md`): the Stack takes a clip address, `temperature` and `pitch_semitones` per speech request instead of `POST/DELETE /v1/voices` (Home is the master of the record), caches the prepared clip per sha256, restores the default voice after a job, shifts pitch with formants kept (numpy and scipy), and fetches the pinned S3TokenizerV2 on the first clip voice; the starter set of eleven voices, the listening gate, the Models and storage rows and the removal of the community browser routes stay open; Stack `modelCatalog.ts`, `speech/mlx_tts_server.py`, `routes/voices.ts`; catalog `voices/starter-voices`; Home Models and storage rows). Pin S3TokenizerV2 (472 MB) and prove it loaded; cache a `Conditionals` per clip sha256 and restore the default after a job; `POST/DELETE /v1/voices`; eleven voices (six CC0 donations, four Kokoro synthetic) passing the section 1.5 listening gate (WER, tags per voice, Jesse's ear); remove the community browser routes. Acceptance: cached first audio within 0.1 s of the default. Sampling temperature (2026-10-20, bot `docs/dev/design-stackchan-voice-2026-10-20.md`, bot main c9b3c1c): when a voice record carries `temperature`, the Stack passes it to Chatterbox Turbo `generate` for that job and restores the engine default after; Turbo ignores `exaggeration` and `cfg_weight`, so they are not exposed. Acceptance (fail-first): a voice with `temperature: 1.05` reaches `generate` with 1.05; a voice without one uses the engine default; a value outside 0.1 to 2.0 is refused at `POST /v1/voices` with a plain message. Temperature also raises pitch (1.25 rose further above the reference), so 1.05 is the practical liveliness ceiling for a clone (bot `docs/dev/design-stackchan-voice-2026-10-20.md`, second-voice section, bot main afd0ab7). Pitch offset: when a voice record carries `pitch_semitones` other than 0, the Stack shifts the rendered audio by that many semitones with formants kept, after generation and before the audio leaves the Stack (the bench used rubberband; the Stack picks the library under its dependency rules, local only). Acceptance (fail-first): a voice with `pitch_semitones: -1` returns audio whose median pitch is about 1 semitone below the same text unshifted; a voice without one skips the shift step entirely; a value outside -12 to 12 is refused at `POST /v1/voices` with a plain message.

## Resource tiers (owner, 2026-10-27)

From [resource-tiers-2026-10-27.md](design/resource-tiers-2026-10-27.md): every generating feature gets Standard, Boost and Max (Max for admins and assigned adults; a teen's grant reaches the teen picture lane only, RULES.md rule 8), plus a system-only Reduced state that simplifies other categories while a Max job runs. Dynamic per hardware class (the Studio first), customizable per slot by an admin, switchable per mode and category, built on the memory note's queue and the Stack governor. Replaces the `coding.home_mode` switch with a Max chat lease. Evaluations first (the note's section 14); nothing is built on a model before its evaluation row is done. Models download only with Jesse's yes; bench rows run one at a time under the machine lock. Reuse check for the whole section: `engines.<role>.choice`, the governor and household queue of the memory note, coding mode's swap transaction and readiness record, the `light` profile, `grant-actions.json`, the model chip, the job cards and the AI & models page. Nothing here adds a queue, ledger, status surface or setting family.

- [ ] **TIER-EVAL-01: Reduced chat** (S, Stack bench). Measure the Qwen3-4B `light`-profile model (and one other 4B to 8B) as chat during a Max window: swap time out and back, memory, whether the Max job must pause for its turns, CHAT-AB-01 including the child turn, the 3-second first-word bar for a spoken turn and the safety rows (rules 13 and 0), the tool-decision measurement (rule 3), and minors' floors (thinking off, no tools). The pattern is MODE-BENCH-01. Mirror: `scripts/bench-isolation.ts`. Acceptance: a decision record in `docs/design/` with the numbers and a pass or fail for Reduced chat; if fail, Max stays at 72 GB. Out of scope: building the swap. Exit: the bench output attached to the record.
- [ ] **TIER-EVAL-02: Reduced voice, including Chatterbox Nano** (M, Stack bench). Bench Chatterbox Nano (110M, MIT, English only) against Pocket TTS and Chatterbox Turbo on MLX: resident memory, time to first audio, streaming yes or no, which runtime works (MLX, MPS, CPU; community Core ML, ONNX, GGUF builds exist), voice closeness to Turbo with the same reference clip, whether household cloned voices carry over. Needs Jesse's yes for the download. Acceptance: a decision record naming the Reduced voice recommendation for p64 and p128 and whether Nano is worth a look as the p16 and p32 default.
